qAndA.answer: Even that tiny sliver of the sun's surface emits intense light that can damage your eyes.
qAndA.question: Why is it dangerous to look at the sun even when 99% of it is covered during an eclipse?

qAndA.answer: An approved solar filter is essential. Regular sunglasses or DIY filters are not sufficient.
qAndA.question: What type of filter is safe to use when looking at a solar eclipse?

qAndA.answer: Yes, but only during totality AND with a proper solar filter securely attached to the front of the device.
qAndA.question: Can you use binoculars or a telescope to view the eclipse?
